directAnswer: St. Caius (also Gaius) was the twenty-eighth bishop of Rome, serving from 283 to 296, in the years before Diocletian’s Great Persecution. Little is known about him beyond his dates and his burial in the Catacomb of St. Callixtus. Later legend makes him a relative of Diocletian and a martyr, but these claims are unreliable.

paras: Caius governed the Roman Church for about thirteen years, a long pontificate for the period. Diocletian came to power in 284, but his persecution did not begin until 303, years after Caius’s death, so the Church continued to enjoy freedom and growth during his time.

The Liber Pontificalis says Caius was a Dalmatian from Salona and claims he established that a cleric must pass through each of the minor orders before becoming a bishop. A later legend makes him a relative of Diocletian, but there is no evidence for this.

Caius was buried in the Catacomb of St. Callixtus, in a section near the papal crypt, where his epitaph was found in the nineteenth century. His legendary martyrdom by beheading does not fit the timeline, and early Roman records list him among bishops rather than martyrs.
His feast day is April 22, shared with Pope St. Soter.

keyFacts: Twenty-eighth bishop of Rome, December 17, 283, to April 22, 296
Reigned during the peace before Diocletian’s persecution
Liber Pontificalis calls him a Dalmatian from Salona
Buried in the Catacomb of St. Callixtus, where his epitaph was found
Feast day April 22, shared with St. Soter

faqs.question: Was Pope St. Caius related to Emperor Diocletian?
faqs.answer: A later legend says so, since both were associated with Dalmatia, but there is no reliable historical evidence for the claim.

faqs.question: Was Pope Caius martyred?
faqs.answer: Legend says he was beheaded, but he died years before Diocletian’s persecution began, and early records do not call him a martyr.
